title: SpaceX testifies before City Council about potential risks of AI
source_used: New York Daily News (full report); Spectrum News NY1 (short text, read)
key_facts: SpaceXAI, Elon Musk's AI company and maker of the Grok chatbot, testified at a New York City Council Technology Committee hearing on Friday 16 Oct 2026, only after being compelled by a subpoena and threatened with further legal action.
NY1 says the company, a subsidiary of Musk's SpaceX, had skipped the previous week's high-profile Council hearing on AI.
Gabriela Castillo Madrid, SpaceXAI's senior manager of global government affairs, testified for the company.

Council Speaker Julie Menin said she could find a sexualized image of herself made with Grok within a second and called it unacceptable; Castillo Madrid said she could not speak to that case but that Grok has 'strict controls' to prevent sexualizing people, including children.
Asked how many people ensure safety standards are followed, Castillo Madrid said 'everybody is in charge of safety'; Menin asked for a number by the end of the testimony.

Devin Kim, who says he was fired from SpaceXAI after raising safety concerns and is suing the company, also testified; Menin told reporters she did not find Castillo Madrid's claim of no knowledge of his firing credible.

Last week executives from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta testified at a Committee of the Whole meeting, and the Council is considering 10 pieces of legislation aimed at regulating the AI industry.
Carmen De La Rosa, chair of the Technology Committee, called the image 'disgusting'.
quote_evidence: How is it that within a second I could find a sexualized image of myself, using Grok?
SpaceXAI testified before the Council only after being compelled to testify with a subpoena and being threatened with further legal action.
The City Council is considering 10 pieces of legislation aimed at regulating the AI industry.
why_it_matters_hint: A major AI company had to answer city lawmakers in public about chatbot safety after resisting a subpoena, while the Council weighs 10 AI bills.
notes: NY1 text (pool source) is only a short teaser with no detail, so the entry is built from the New York Daily News report; NY1 is credited in the notes only. Follow-up of the 14 Oct 2026 edition item 'SpaceX agrees to testify to NYC Council about AI safety after receiving subpoena' (CNBC). Crain's New York headline says Grok produced the image 'in under 30 seconds' while Menin is quoted as saying 'within a second', so the entry says 'within seconds'. CNBC and Quartz not opened (403).
